_comment: Example .mcp.json for an authorized bug bounty engagement.
THE ONE RULE: never combine a target-touching server with a data-bearing or
write-capable server in the same session. Toxic data flows are ~37% of real MCP
findings and ~100% of the ways an agentic hunter gets banned.
So: run EITHER the target-touching profile (burp + playwright) OR the
data profile (hackerone + github). Not both at once.
Put this at your engagement repo root (scope: project) so scope travels with the
engagement and is reviewable in git. Keep credentials in the environment, never
as literals here - this file gets committed.
Gotcha: 'url' without 'type' is parsed as stdio and fails. Always set type.
Env expansion happens at CONNECTION time, so export before launching claude.

burp._comment: Official PortSwigger MCP. Disable 'allow config editing' in the Burp MCP tab, and deny the set_*_options tools in settings.json - they merge arbitrary JSON into Burp config. Scope auto-approve to your target, never '*'.

playwright._comment: Deterministic multi-step browser control - needed for the two-account IDOR oracle and for proving XSS actually executes. Use a throwaway profile, never your logged-in daily one.

semgrep._comment: Runs entirely locally over stdio - nothing leaves your machine. Lowest-risk code analysis. Do NOT use the hosted mcp.semgrep.ai for client work; it ships your code off-box.

hackerone._comment: Official, GA, READ-ONLY by construction - cannot modify reports or program settings. Lowest-risk server available. Use for scope ingestion, duplicate checking, regression leads. NOTE: each client has its own OAuth client_id; the Claude Code CLI id differs from Desktop/Web. Run `claude mcp login hackerone`. Verify the current URL against docs.hackerone.com.

github._comment: Only for source-available targets whose org is explicitly in scope. Scope the PAT ruthlessly - this is the single most dangerous token to hand an agent. NEVER in the same session as target-touching tools.

censys._comment: Passive only. Calls burn credits - an agent loop can drain a quota in minutes. Cost is the real risk here, not security.
